product: ELM Surfaces Formed collection, Hexagon Tile in Sand (Matte / Raw / Chiseled mix)

atlas.hexagon: flat-top, 10.000 in across flats (assumed reading of 10 x 10)

revit.bump_amount_note: start at 0.5 (repo convention 0.3-0.5 for dimensional tiles); the joint uses the full 0-65535 range and Raw about 65 %, so lower towards 0.3 if joints read too heavy. Not validated in Revit in this trial.

joint_rgb_source: median of the darkest 20 % of render pixels on the joint centreline

mix_ratio_render.note: counted in the render's 45 classified cells: faces with >= 99 % of their inset interior visible count 1; the weighted count adds partly visible faces by visible fraction

relief_terms_mm.chiseled_depth_modulation: channel depth x (1 + m), m = render groove amplitude modulation, clipped +-0.6

chiseled_geometry.channel_shape: ((1 + cos 2 pi phi) / 2) ** 1.65, crest plane at 0
chiseled_geometry.rotation_convention: rotation_deg is the hexagon rotation of the vertical-groove face, counter-clockwise as viewed: 0 -> vertical, 60 -> 30 deg image angle ('\'), 300 -> 150 deg image angle ('/')

quilting.note: duplicate_percent = share of quilted face pixels whose render source pixel also appears at another output location (same or other face), counting both copies; the pools are smaller than the atlas needs (Raw: ~8.7 render faces of pixels for 11 atlas faces, Matte ~25 for 32, Chiseled 9 for 13). The three Chiseled class pools are the same 9 render faces rotated, so they also share content across classes, under the rebuilt grooves.

ghost_joint_check.note: oriented (0/60/120 deg, 1 in) dark-line filter on colour luma; a copied render joint inside a Matte or Raw face would score near the joint median. Chiseled faces are listed separately: their 30/90/150 deg grooves partly excite the filter.

wrap_seam_steps.method: mean |difference| between the last and first pixel line of the image (the wrap seam) vs the mean |difference| one pixel either side of the seam; ratio ~1 means no seam
